chapterName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE)

questions.question: What word did French scholars coin for the endless hunt for Hannibal's Alpine route?
questions.explanation: 'Hannibalism' describes chasing a question that may have no answer. Polybius gives just three place names, and no weapons or camps have been found.
questions.sourceQuote: French scholars coined a word, 'Hannibalism', for chasing a question that may have no answer.

questions.question: What is Hannibal's famous manoeuvre at Cannae called?
questions.explanation: Hannibal's African infantry closed in on both flanks while his cavalry struck the Roman rear. This pincer movement has been studied by generals ever since.
questions.sourceQuote: This 'double envelopment', or pincer movement, has been studied by generals ever since.

questions.question: After Hannibal's cavalry won at the Ticinus in 218 BC, who declared for him?
questions.explanation: After the cavalry victory at the Ticinus, most Gallic tribes declared for Hannibal. More Gauls flocked to him after the Trebia, swelling his army to some 60,000.
questions.sourceQuote: In late November 218 BC his cavalry routed Roman horsemen at the Ticinus, a river in the Po valley, and most Gallic tribes declared for him.

questions.question: How old was Hannibal when the army's officers chose him as their commander in 221 BC?
questions.explanation: Hannibal was just 26 when the officers picked him. He took over after his brother-in-law, the previous commander, was murdered.
questions.sourceQuote: When the son-in-law was murdered in 221 BC, the army's officers chose Hannibal, then just 26, as their commander.

questions.question: Where did Hannibal ambush a Roman army in 217 BC, killing the consul leading it?
questions.explanation: At Lake Trasimene in central Italy, some 15,000 Romans died, the consul among them. Another 10,000 were captured.
questions.sourceQuote: At Lake Trasimene in central Italy he sprang an ambush.

questions.question: How did Hannibal get his elephants across the Rhône?
options: By marching them upstream to the river's source
By swimming them across a shallow ford
Over a stone bridge built by his engineers
On rafts covered with earth so they seemed on land
questions.explanation: The rafts were covered with earth so the elephants believed they were still on land. Meanwhile a detachment crossed upstream to attack the hostile Gauls from behind.
questions.sourceQuote: His elephants were coaxed onto rafts covered with earth, so they believed they were still on land.

questions.question: What emergency office did Roman voters give Fabius after the defeat at Trasimene?
questions.explanation: A dictator held supreme command for a limited term. Fabius was the same senator who had carried Rome's ultimatum to Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: The voters turned to Fabius Maximus, the senator who had carried Rome's ultimatum to Carthage, and made him dictator, an emergency office giving one man supreme command for a limited term.

questions.question: Who reportedly told Hannibal, 'You know how to win a victory, Hannibal; you do not know how to use it'?
questions.explanation: His cavalry commander is said to have urged a march on Rome after Cannae. Modern historians note that Hannibal's battered army was in no state to assault the city.
questions.sourceQuote: His cavalry commander urged a march on Rome and, it is said, cried: 'You know how to win a victory, Hannibal; you do not know how to use it.'

questions.question: Which Spanish city, which had an agreement with Rome, did Hannibal besiege in 219 BC?
questions.explanation: Hannibal besieged Saguntum after he had conquered the other tribes south of the Ebro. The city held out for eight months, and Rome sent no help.
questions.sourceQuote: When that failed, he besieged the city in 219 BC.

questions.question: How did the Greek historian Polybius come to live in Rome?
options: He was taken there as a hostage
He served there as an ambassador
He was hired as a tutor by the Senate
questions.explanation: Polybius was taken to Rome as a hostage in 167 BC. He interviewed participants from both sides, and modern historians generally trust him.
questions.sourceQuote: Polybius was a Greek taken to Rome as a hostage in 167 BC, who wrote after 146 BC.
